source_title: An Agent Based Simulation Tool for Scheduling Emergency Department Physicians
locator: Methods, Table 1 (site-specific settings); Methods, patient arrival input description
source_setting: Single 32-bed ED in a 520-bed urban Level I trauma center, Utah, United States; about 40,000 annual visits.
source_period: Site ED operations; observed door-to-doctor comparison covered first 10 months of 2007. Table 1 does not provide a distinct parameter-estimation period.
source_n: Average weekly arrivals parameter corresponds to about 40,000 annual visits; 2007 door-to-doctor sample size not reported in extract.
source_evidence_basis: Author-reported site-specific input supplied to the simulation, derived from average weekly counts; this is a modeled input, not a separately tabulated raw observed distribution.
limitations: Single older academic trauma center. Authors describe weekly arrivals as a 168-hour heterogeneous Poisson process, estimating each hour-of-week rate from average counts for that hour; no numerical 168-hour rate vector or patient-level arrival distribution is published in the extract. external_proxy_candidate; qualitative confidence: moderate as a documented comparator, low for transfer to a local hospital.

source_title: An Agent Based Simulation Tool for Scheduling Emergency Department Physicians
source_setting: Single 32-bed ED in a 520-bed urban Level I trauma center, Utah, United States; about 40,000 annual visits.
source_period: Model input used for the study simulation; observed validation comparison covered first 10 months of 2007. Exact admission-rate estimation interval is not specified.
source_n: Not separately reported for the rate; site volume approximately 40,000 visits/year.
source_evidence_basis: Author-reported site-specific simulation input; treated as a model parameter rather than an independently presented raw-data estimate.
limitations: Admission mix varies by acuity, service availability, and hospital capacity; one site and period. Do not interpret as a local or nationally representative admission probability. external_proxy_candidate; qualitative confidence: moderate as a source-specific parameter, low for transfer.

source_title: An Agent Based Simulation Tool for Scheduling Emergency Department Physicians
locator: Results, comparison of observed and simulated door-to-doctor distributions
source_setting: Single 32-bed ED in a 520-bed urban Level I trauma center, Utah, United States.
source_period: First 10 months of 2007 for observed door-to-doctor times.
source_n: Not reported for the observed door-to-doctor sample.
quantity: Observed door-to-doctor time, median and interquartile range
source_evidence_basis: Observed site data used to validate the simulation; authors report median, mean, and IQR separately from simulated output.
limitations: This is waiting to initial physician evaluation, not total ED length of stay or active diagnostic/treatment service duration. Historical single-site data, sample size unavailable. external_proxy_candidate; qualitative confidence: moderate as an observed comparator, low for transfer.

source_title: Hospital Factors Impact Variation in Emergency Department Length of Stay More Than Physician Factors
locator: Methods, Study Setting and Population; Table 2; Table 3
source_setting: Urban county hospital, Corpus Christi, Texas, United States; Level II trauma center with 41,000 annual visits and 18% admission rate.
source_period: Daily interval averages collected over one year; exact calendar dates are not stated in the opened article text. Authors compare daily averages above/below the 2008 national median LOS threshold of 154 minutes.
source_n: Approximately 41,000 annual visits; number of daily observations not stated.
quantity: Door-to-room median by lower- versus higher-LOS day group
source_evidence_basis: Measured daily ED information-system interval averages; reported medians and SDs for two groups, not a patient-level distribution. Door-to-room is arrival to an available treatment room.
limitations: The 154-minute grouping threshold is the 2008 NHAMCS national median; these values are from one hospital and are not national arrival-to-room priors. Confounders such as radiology, laboratory, and acuity markers were not included. external_proxy_candidate; qualitative confidence: moderate for a site-specific operational comparator, low for transfer.

source_title: Hospital Factors Impact Variation in Emergency Department Length of Stay More Than Physician Factors
source_setting: Urban county hospital, Corpus Christi, Texas, United States; Level II trauma center, 41,000 annual visits; admission rate 18%.
source_period: Daily interval averages collected over one year; calendar dates not stated in the opened article text.
source_n: Approximately 41,000 annual visits; number of daily observations not stated.
quantity: Admit decision to ED departure median, an ED boarding interval
source_evidence_basis: Measured operational interval from admission decision until patient physically departs the ED treatment area; Table 2 reports medians and SDs by ED LOS group.
limitations: This is boarding after the admission decision, not inpatient bed turnaround from bed request, and group membership is based on whole-day discharged-patient LOS versus the national 154-minute threshold. It is not active clinical service time. external_proxy_candidate; qualitative confidence: moderate for observed site boarding, low for transfer.

source_title: Waiting for Triage: Unmeasured Time in Patient Flow
locator: Methods and Results; arrival-to-triage results for patients requiring greeting before triage
source_setting: Urban academic tertiary ED, Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, Boston, Massachusetts, United States; approximately 54,000 annual visits.
source_n: 50,576 total visits; 7,795 (15.4%) did not go directly to bed or triage and were included in the pre-triage waiting subgroup.
quantity: Arrival-to-triage wait among patients who did not go directly to bed or triage
source_evidence_basis: Directly observed arrival time and routine triage time; subgroup distribution reported as median, IQR, and range.
limitations: Conditional on the 15.4% subgroup that did not proceed directly to a bed or triage; not a general door-to-provider estimate. Single-site workflow may differ substantially. external_proxy_candidate; qualitative confidence: moderate for its observed subgroup, low for transfer.
